item.title: Jacksons Hill Sale Scrutiny: Victoria defends A$1m Nine deal; MP demands transparency
item.description: The sale of Jacksons Hill, a historic psychiatric hospital, to Channel Nine for A$1 million has sparked significant debate. Critics argue over the valuation and the absence of a competitive bidding process. With three heritage-listed buildings included, any redevelopment will demand meticulous restoration to comply with heritage regulations. The government's intent is to maintain the site's legacy while also promoting investment in the surrounding area.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida protects 1,034-acre ranch once owned by governor in $6.52m conservation deal
item.description: Florida has approved a $6.52 million conservation easement to protect Limestone Creek Ranch from development. The 1,034-acre property has been involved in cattle ranching for over 70 years. This agreement allows continued agricultural operations while preventing future development on the land. Governor Ron DeSantis emphasized the importance of protecting Florida's unique lands and waters. The initiative is part of a broader effort involving over 10,770 acres across the state.

item.title: Houthis claim Saudi airport attack that killed 12 as Middle East tensions rise
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen said Sunday's projectile hit Terminal 4 of the airport, causing a fire. Saudi air defences also intercepted a cruise missile near the airport, although authorities did not immediately provide further details about the latest incident. The airport remained closed following Saturday's attack.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: ‘Our seas, our land’: Sri Lanka assures India against hostile acts from its territory
item.description: Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has stressed that his country will not allow its territory for hostile actions. He reiterated the commitment to a non-aligned foreign policy amid the US-Iran conflict and rejected military requests from both sides. Dissanayake emphasized humanitarian assistance will be provided if needed. Security cooperation with India was also reaffirmed during a recent meeting with Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Ukraine steps up attacks on Russian tech infrastructure, damages third data center
item.description: A recent drone strike by Ukraine has damaged a Yandex data center in Vladimir, disrupting operations and causing service outages in taxi and banking sectors across multiple cities. This incident is part of a series of continuous aerial assaults on Yandex facilities, raising alarms over rising diesel prices in the U.S. Additionally, a drone strike in Bryansk has resulted in casualties, intensifying regional tensions.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Zelenskyy says ready to hold Ukraine elections if Russia offers 60-day ceasefire
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky suggested organizing elections if a 60-day ceasefire with Russia is established. He reacted to criticisms from Donald Trump regarding his leadership and military actions. Zelensky emphasized that the decision of Ukraine's leadership lies with its people, not external figures. He acknowledged an announcement of an energy ceasefire, but stated it was news to him.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Egypt’s ancient Fayoum portraits to be exhibited abroad for first time
item.description: Egypt recently revealed a restored version of the Tondo of the Two Brothers painting at a press conference. The painting, created during the second century, is part of the Fayoum portrait collection. Italian and Egyptian experts collaborated for three weeks on the restoration project in Tahrir. A major exhibition will showcase the restored portraits in Rome from November through May 2027.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Rare Ming dynasty pomegranate box bought for £19 in 1946 sells for £288,000 after attic discovery
item.description: A 15th-century Chinese enamel box, originally bought for £19, sold for £288,000 at an auction. The box was rediscovered in a family attic where it remained unnoticed for decades. Major Edward Copleston Radcliffe acquired the box in 1946, and it was assessed by Dreweatts auction house. Experts confirmed the box's significance, linking it to the rare Xuande-marked pomegranate boxes.

item.title: Houthis blame Saudi Arabia for another strike on Sanaa's airport
item.description: Air strikes were reported by Houthi-aligned media on Houthi-held territories including Sanaa international airport. The Saudi-led coalition condemned an earlier attack that caused civilian casualties and incurred fatalities from different nationalities. Houthi spokesperson warned against the use of Saudi airspace by airlines, asserting their military strategy. The conflict between the two sides has escalated, leading to significant civilian impacts and suffering.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: 'Good for Americans': US treasury secretary defends Russia diesel deal, cites 'legal authority'
item.description: Defending the diesel supply agreement with Russia, Scott Bessent highlights the Trump administration's strategy to alleviate fuel prices. The deal initiates with more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel heading from Russia, with an additional 3 million tonnes expected shortly. The US Treasury Secretary assures that the decision rests on legal foundations, with promising implications for both American consumers and the international trading landscape.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Florida family’s 498-acre cattle ranch protected from development through $7.48m conservation easement
item.description: A 498-acre cattle ranch known as Turnpike Dairy has been protected from future development through a conservation easement. The agreement allows the managing family to continue agricultural operations on the property. Martin County contributed $3.74 million towards the $7.48 million deal to preserve the land. This conservation effort is part of Florida’s Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, which protects working farms.

item.title: US air museum to reopen as storm-damaged World War II hangar finds new owner for $1
item.description: An 83-year-old World War II-era blimp hangar in Oregon, US, was sold for just $1 after a storm tore a 200-foot hole in its roof in December 2025. The historic building, which houses the Tillamook Air Museum, was purchased by a nonprofit organisation and is set to reopen on October 29 after nearly 10 months of closure.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Federal judge halts ICE detention centre construction at California site over environmental review
item.description: A federal judge has granted a preliminary injunction halting construction of an ICE facility near Gilroy, California. The ruling came in response to a lawsuit filed by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and Santa Clara County. They argued that construction began without an adequate environmental assessment or consultations with local officials. Environmental risks associated with the site, such as septic system capacity and hazardous materials, were also raised.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV to undergo lung surgery ahead of major South America trip in November
item.description: Addressing the public during his traditional Sunday noon blessing, Leo thanked those who had expressed concern and asked them to keep him in their prayers. The pope said the abnormality had been detected at an early stage and was localised, adding that he had decided to proceed with surgery on medical advice.
